findings.title: SUB.B1 — Appendix 1 CS-FSTD(A).300 FSTD Standards — 3. Visual System — d.1 Visual system free of discontinuities
findings.description:
The visual system does not have the projector "blending/overlap" correctly adjusted, particularly between the projector covering the central and right areas of the screen, since a double image is visible. This effect causes confusion, especially during the approach phase with wind from the left, which results in the landing runway appearing within the overlap zone.

This same defect was already detected during the previous evaluation and was assumed to have been corrected based on the evidence submitted at the time. There is no evidence that the simulator's preventive maintenance procedures include a regular check of the projector blending adjustment.
findings.resolution:
A new USB Dongle with its corresponding software license has been purchased. Once installed, the system will be recalibrated and the projector positions adjusted to restore optimal operating conditions.

Additionally, the preventive maintenance plan will be updated to include a new monthly task covering verification of blending status, presence and operation of the license USB Dongle, and checking of projector alignment and positioning, in order to prevent recurrence of this issue.

findings.title: SUB.B2 — Appendix 1 CS-FSTD(A).300 FSTD Standards — 1. General — a.6 Flight instruments in correct location
findings.description: The PFD becomes detached from its correct position, which means that the lower part of the screen, with various data-presentation MENU options, cannot be seen properly because it is hidden by the bezel.
findings.resolution:
A technical intervention will be carried out to replace the current fastening system or implement an alternative solution that permanently ensures correct attachment of the screen. Although previous correction attempts have been made, they have not fully resolved the issue, so more robust fastening options will be evaluated.

As an additional preventive measure, informational signage has been placed next to the screen indicating that the device does not have touch functionality. This action aims to prevent students from mishandling the screen, thereby reducing the mechanical stress on the fastening system and minimizing the risk of recurrence.

findings.title: SUB.B3 — Appendix 1 CS-FSTD(A).300 FSTD Standards — 1. General — g.1 System operation
findings.description:
During the stall-entry test, with a weight of approximately 2,600 lb and an altitude of 5,000 ft, the Stall Warning activates almost simultaneously with the actual stall, without the minimum required anticipation margin of at least 5 kt, both in clean configuration and with flaps in landing position. The stall warning only sounds with a more acceptable margin for the flaps-in-takeoff-position configuration:

- Clean Configuration (FLAPS UP): Stall warning IAS 67 kt, Stall IAS 67 kt
- FLAP Take Off: Stall warning IAS 64 kt, Stall IAS 64 kt
- FLAP LANDING: Stall warning IAS 62 kt, Stall IAS 56 kt.

This same defect was already detected during the previous evaluation, and it was assumed to have been corrected based on the evidence submitted. It has malfunctioned again.

According to MQTG test 2c(8b)1, performed at a weight of 2,700 lb and an altitude of 3,000 ft with Flaps UP and L/G down, the Stall Warning activates at a CAS of 70 kt and the minimum speed reached is CAS 60 kt.

According to MQTG test 2c(8b)2, performed at a weight of 2,700 lb and an altitude of 3,000 ft with Flaps T/O and L/G down, the Stall Warning activates at a CAS of 66 kt and the minimum speed reached is CAS 59 kt.
findings.resolution:
A technical incident will be opened with the simulator manufacturer, providing the results obtained during the evaluation and reference to the requirements established in the applicable MQTG tests.

The manufacturer must analyze the configuration and parameterization of the stall-warning system, and review the modifications implemented during previous work related to correcting the QTG, in order to identify the origin of the discrepancy.

Once the technical cause is determined, the necessary corrections will be implemented and new functional and subjective tests will be carried out to verify that the Stall Warning activates with the anticipation required in all applicable flight configurations and within the tolerances established by the MQTG.

After the intervention, the results of the verifications performed will be documented.

findings.title: SUB.B4 — Appendix 1 CS-FSTD(A).300 FSTD Standards — 1. General — i.1 Control forces corresponding to the replicated aircraft type
findings.description: The force required to move the Roll control appears higher than would be expected for this type of aircraft, directly affecting control precision and pilot workload. Although according to the recurrent QTG 2a(2), the result matches the MQTG.
findings.resolution:
QTG test 2.a.(2), corresponding to the aileron control force, will be repeated on each affected simulator. Additionally, an independent manual measurement will be carried out using a dynamometer, verifying at least the force required to reach maximum deflection of the aileron control. The values obtained through manual measurement will be compared with the results recorded by the automatic QTG test, in order to validate the accuracy of the simulator's measurements and confirm that the control forces fall within acceptable tolerances.

Depending on the results obtained: if the difference between both measurements is minimal and compatible with the established tolerances, closure will proceed. If significant deviations are detected, a technical incident will be opened with the manufacturer to investigate the origin of the problem.

findings.title: SUB.C1 — Appendix 1 CS-FSTD(A).300 FSTD Standards — 1. General — a.6 Switches functioning correctly
findings.description: The Autopilot disconnect button on the control yoke does not work. To disconnect the AP, the AP-MASTER must be switched off, or the controls must be moved to override the AP's force.
findings.resolution:
An inspection of the system will be carried out to determine the exact origin of the fault, checking the condition of the button, the wiring, the connectors, and correct signal reception by the control system.

Once the cause has been identified, the defective components will be repaired or replaced. After the intervention, functional tests will be performed to confirm that the Autopilot disconnect button operates correctly and that disconnection occurs as expected.

findings.title: SUB.C2 — Appendix 1 CS-FSTD(A).300 FSTD Standards — 1. General — a.6 Instruments functioning correctly
findings.description:
When the simulator is switched on, the EFIS STANDBY instrument appears off-center and is not displayed correctly. It is necessary to remove the simulator's forward cowling to access the instrument's electronic control board and reset it manually so that it displays correctly, then reinstall the cowling.

This defect was identified during the FSTD Organization's own most recent functional and subjective test, carried out on 24-04-2026, but was not recorded in the HIL at the time of the AESA inspection.
findings.resolution:
The incident will be formally reported to the simulator manufacturer so that it can carry out a technical analysis of the EFIS STANDBY instrument, its electronic control board, and the associated initialization procedures.

The manufacturer must identify the cause of the fault and propose a permanent solution that eliminates the need for manual resets via physical access to the hardware.

Once the correction has been implemented, repeated startup tests will be carried out to verify that the instrument initializes correctly every time and maintains a proper display without the need for manual intervention.

The fault will be reported in the HIL.

findings.title: OBJ.B1 — Appendix 1 CS-FSTD(A).300 FSTD Standards — 1. General — e.3 Updated navigation database
findings.description:
The last three updates of the Navigation Database have not been performed at the maximum three-month interval established by the regulation, as observed in the NAVDATA UPDATES — Changes Record log:

- Cycle 2506 updated on 14/06/2025
- Cycle 2510 updated on 15/10/2025, after 4 months had elapsed
- Cycle 2602 updated on 12/02/2026, after 4 months had elapsed
- Current cycle installed on 20/05/2026, after slightly more than 3 months had elapsed

However, despite the above evidence, internal audit PVC-13, carried out on 10/04/2026, in question 3 of the FSTD-3 area of that audit, indicates that point "2. Navigation databases are reviewed. Validity should not exceed 3 months" is compliant.
findings.resolution:
The manufacturer will be formally notified of the need to ensure that Navigation Database updates are carried out within the deadlines established by the regulation, defining a communication and planning procedure that provides advance notice of scheduled update dates.

Additionally, the FSTD Organization will implement a specific internal control system to monitor the currency of NAVDATA. This control will include periodic review of the installation date and current AIRAC cycle, as well as the generation of preventive alerts as the maximum permitted limit approaches.

Likewise, the internal audit program and the associated checklists will be reviewed to strengthen documentary verification of navigation database currency, preventing similar situations from going undetected during future audits.

findings.title: OBJ.B2 — AMC1.FSTD(A).300 Qualification Basis — point (a)(ii)(I)(j): Validation Test Results
findings.description:
In the following recurrent QTGs, performed by the FSTD Organization in the cycle, the irregularities indicated below are observed:

- Test 2c(1)1 Power Change Dynamics: the Bank Angle chart behaves incorrectly ("CT&M") relative to the approved MQTG result.
- Test 2c(2)3 Flap Change Force TO and Test 2c(2)4 Flap Change Force APCH: the ELEV ANGL chart of the MQTG curve is not the same as the one shown on the approved MQTG.
- Test 2c(4)1 Gear Change Dynamics TO: the Bank Angle chart behaves incorrectly ("CT&M") relative to the approved MQTG result.
- Test 2c(5)1 Long Trim Cruise Cruise: the first snapshot has a small R/C of 16.29 ft/min, which is acceptable, but the second and third snapshots have an R/C > 100 ft/min in descent, when it should be level flight at constant altitude. In the MQTG, the values for snapshots 2 and 3 were acceptable.
- In all three Test 2c(8b)x Approach-to-Stall tests, the force values at the moment of Stall Warning are missing.
- Test 2d(1) Vmca during TO: the MQTG values are missing in one column, preventing comparison.
findings.resolution:
The affected QTGs will be repeated using the approved version of the MQTG and carefully verifying all data generated and transcribed in the corresponding records.

The new results will be independently reviewed to confirm whether the discrepancies detected correspond solely to documentary errors or whether there is any real deviation in the results obtained by the simulator.

In parallel, the manufacturer will be notified of the situation so that it can analyze the possible existence of errors in report generation, test templates, or software modifications that may have affected the presentation or integrity of the validation data.

Likewise, the internal QTG execution and verification procedure will be reviewed in order to strengthen documentary quality controls prior to formal acceptance of results.

findings.title: OBJ.B3 — AMC1.FSTD(A).300 Qualification Basis — point (a)(ii)(I)(j): Validation Test Results
findings.description:
In the following QTGs, repeated on 28-05-2026 during AESA's recurrent evaluation, the following irregularities are observed:

- Test 1c(1) Normal Climb All Engines Operating: the "Rate of Climb" parameter is out of tolerance, below what is observed on the MQTG. In addition, the altitude at the start of the test is incorrect.
- Test 2c(2)2 Flap Change Dynamics during Approach: the Bank Angle chart behaves incorrectly ("CT&M") relative to the approved MQTG result.
- Test 2c(8b)2 Approach to Stall — Approach Configuration: the pitch control force value at the moment of Stall Warning does not appear.
- Test 2c(9) Phugoid Dynamics during Cruise: the Bank Angle chart behaves incorrectly ("CT&M") relative to the approved MQTG result.
- Test 2d(2)2 Roll Response Rate during Approach: the Calibrated Airspeed chart behaves incorrectly ("CT&M") relative to the approved MQTG result.
- Test 2d(5)2 Engine Inoperative Trim — Approach: the column with the MQTG results does not appear. In the recurrent test performed by the FSTD Organization in the cycle, the column with the MQTG values does appear.
findings.resolution:
The manufacturer will be formally notified of the full set of discrepancies detected during the recurrent evaluation. A thorough review will be requested of the simulator configuration, the changes implemented during the most recent maintenance work, and the parameters associated with the affected QTG tests, with the aim of identifying possible side effects arising from previous modifications.

The affected QTGs will subsequently be repeated to verify that the detected discrepancies have been eliminated and to confirm that the results obtained are consistent with the approved MQTG reference values.

Additionally, the FSTD Organization will review its configuration-control and external-modification-tracking process to strengthen oversight of manufacturer changes and minimize the risk of recurrence of similar incidents.

findings.title: OBJ.B4 — AMC1.FSTD(A).300 Qualification Basis — point (a)(ii)(I)(j): Validation Test Results / AMC1.FSTD(A).300 point (a)(6) MQTG Content
findings.description:
During the evaluation of the Major Modification for the HW & SW change requested by the FSTD Organization in 2025 (see AESA file FSTD 0116-2025 MOD-2025-13), discrepancy OBJ.B3 was already detected, noting that the MQTG did not include, in the various Test 2.c.(8b).X of Approach-to-Stall, the pitch control force result at the moment the Stall Warning activates.

According to the documentation submitted by the FSTD Organization via the Electronic Registry Office on 01/09/2025, which included a new corrected version of the MQTG, that new version showed that discrepancy OBJ.B3 had been corrected, as the pitch control force value at the moment of Stall Warning was now included.

However, in the latest version of the MQTG sent to AESA via a download link through an email sent on 07/10/2025 — the version ultimately approved by AESA, a copy of which the FSTD Organization holds — the pitch control force value at the moment of Stall Warning has once again disappeared from that version.
findings.resolution:
A technical clarification will be requested from the manufacturer regarding the changes made and the justification for the disappearance of this data in the recurrent version.

Additionally, the internal documentary-control and configuration-management procedure will be reviewed to strengthen traceability of future modifications and to ensure that corrected discrepancies do not reappear in later versions of the documentation.

findings.title: SUB.B5 — Appendix 1 CS-FSTD(A).300 FSTD Standards — 1. General — a.6 Representative secondary flight controls
findings.description: It is observed that, with the control column fully in the "Nose Down" position, the pitch trim, both in cruise flight and even during the final approach and landing phase with flaps in LAND configuration and low speed, despite the CG (Center of Gravity) being fairly forward (approximately 11%), continues to require significant nose-up force and it is impossible to keep it trimmed. In a landing configuration, even with the pitch control trim in the extreme "Nose Down" position, the aircraft still has a slight tendency to raise the nose and it is impossible to keep it trimmed.
findings.resolution: The incident will be formally reported to the simulator manufacturer. Once the origin of the discrepancy has been identified, the manufacturer must implement the necessary corrections. Functional and subjective tests will subsequently be carried out to verify that the trim system allows the aircraft to be correctly trimmed in all normal flight configurations and within the expected center-of-gravity ranges.

findings.title: SUB.B6 — Appendix 1 CS-FSTD(A).300 FSTD Standards — 1. General — c.1 Flight dynamics model with correct center-of-gravity effects, among others
findings.description:
Strange behavior is observed in the variation of the Center of Gravity with weight. It is observed that as the aircraft is loaded from the rear, the center of gravity moves forward.

- With >80% fuel in each tank, 1 pilot + 1 front passenger: Gross W = 2149.2 lbs, cg = 19.8% MAC
- With >80% fuel in each tank, 1 pilot + 1 front + 1 rear passenger: Gross W = 2325.6 lbs, cg = 15.3% MAC
- With >80% fuel in each tank, 1 pilot + 1 front + 2 rear passengers: Gross W = 2502.0 lbs, cg = 11.1% MAC
findings.resolution: The incident will be formally communicated to the simulator manufacturer. A complete review of the algorithms will be requested. Once the technical cause has been identified, the manufacturer must implement the necessary corrections. New subjective tests will subsequently be carried out with different loading and fuel configurations to verify that the Center of Gravity variations respond consistently to the aircraft's mass distribution and are consistent with the reference documentation.

findings.title: SUB.B7 — Appendix 1 CS-FSTD(A).300 FSTD Standards — 1. General — c.1 Flight dynamics model with correct temperature effects, among others
findings.description:
When performing the VOR approach to runway 01 at GCFV-Fuerteventura, with a temperature of -30ºC (ISA -45º) and QNH 1013, consistent with what was selected on the IOS, and flying the approach precisely to the DME-vs-Altitude table published on the instrument approach chart, without applying a correction for low temperature, the PAPI indication is at all times two white lights and two red lights, meaning that the aircraft is on a correct 3° geometric glidepath. 

However, it would be expected that the PAPI indication would show that the aircraft is flying closer to the ground than the 3° geometric glidepath at all times, given how cold the atmosphere is and given that the cold-atmosphere correction to the altitude indicated on the altimeter was not applied.
findings.resolution:
A technical inquiry will be opened with the simulator manufacturer to determine whether the modelling of cold-temperature effects on true altitude and visual approach aids is implemented in accordance with applicable requirements.

The manufacturer must analyze the observed behavior, verify the capabilities and limitations of the simulation platform used, and confirm whether any configuration, update, or modification exists that would allow the cold-atmosphere effects during instrument approaches to be correctly reproduced.

Once the technical response has been received, the need to implement corrections, updates, or compensatory measures will be evaluated, and new subjective tests will be carried out to verify the simulator's behavior in this scenario.

- Test 2d(4)2 Spiral Stability — Cruise Left: the "Calibrated Airspeed" chart shows a fairly different speed evolution compared to the MQTG data, and the "Bank Angle" parameter goes out of tolerance from second 30 onward, behaving incorrectly ("CT&M") relative to the approved MQTG result.

findings.title: OBJ.B4 — AMC1.FSTD(A).300 Qualification Basis — point (a)(ii)(I)(j): Validation Test Results / AMC1.FSTD(A).300 point (a)(6) MQTG Content
findings.description:
During the automatic repetition of QTG 2c(8b)1 Approach to Stall — Climb Configuration, performed during AESA's recurrent evaluation on 28-05-2026, the indicated airspeed information displayed on the PFD during the Approach-to-Stall phase is recorded on video.

It is observed that, both in the QTG repeated on 28-05-2026 and in the MQTG, the Calibrated Airspeed value at the moment the Stall Warning activates is approximately 60 kt. However, in the video it is observed that the indicated airspeed value on the PFD is 47 kt at the moment the Stall Warning sounds, which is also the moment the aircraft stalls.
findings.resolution:
The discrepancy will be forwarded to the manufacturer, along with the QTG results, the applicable MQTG documentation, and the video recording made during the evaluation.

A technical analysis will be requested to verify the consistency between the speeds displayed on the flight instruments, the parameters recorded by the QTGs, and the values used by the flight model during stall-approach maneuvers.

The manufacturer must identify the origin of the discrepancy and determine whether there is a configuration, parameterization, or integration problem between the display systems and the data-acquisition systems used for validation tests.

Once the necessary corrective actions have been implemented, the affected QTG will be repeated and a new verification will be carried out by video recording to confirm consistency between the values shown in the cockpit and the results recorded in the validation tests.

findings.title: SUB.B1 Apéndice 1 CS FSTD(A).300 Estándares FSTD-3.Sistema Visual-d.1: Visual sin discontinuidades
findings.description: Se debe mejorar el solape/”Blending” entre el proyector hacia el lado izquierdo y hacia el frontal, pues en la zona de solape se ve doble imagen.
findings.resolution: Se procederá al reajuste de la posición del proyector izquierdo para optimizar su alineación con el proyector frontal.
findings.closureEvidence:
Se aportarán fotos del sistema visual tras el reajuste del proyector.

SE ACEPTA, PERO SE REQUIEREN ACCIONES CORRECTORAS/PREVENTIVAS ADICIONALES.
PENDIENTE DE EVIDENCIA PARA CIERRE

Se considera que no se necesitan tres meses desde la fecha de la inspección para solucionar este problema. Se considera suficiente disponer de un mes desde la emisión del Acta de Inspección para el ajuste del blending.

findings.title: SUB.B2 Apéndice 1 CS FSTD(A).300 Estándares FSTD-1.General-g.1: Funcionamiento de Sistemas.
findings.description:
Cuando se activa el fallo de fuego en APU, el fuego no se extingue:

-	Ni con el avión en vuelo, después de completar todos los pasos del ECAM, saltando el “maneral” de fuego de APU en el Overhead Panel, activando la descarga del agente extintor del APU, y poniendo el Master Switch del APU en OFF.
findings.resolution: Si resultara ser un fallo en la lógica del sistema realizado por el fabricante, y se implementara una actualización de software, posteriormente a esa se realizarán pruebas funcionales para verificar el correcto funcionamiento tanto en operaciones en tierra como en vuelo.
findings.closureEvidence:
10-08-2026
SE ACEPTA
PENDIENTE DE EVIDENCIA PARA CIERRE

La discrepancia se podrá cerrar, en ese caso, presentando el HIL-Listado de diferidos como evidencia, con la anotación del fallo.

Si el fabricante confirma que es así como lo ha simulado, que el fuego de APU no se apaga, entonces se deberá solicitar al fabricante que describa correctamente este fallo en el documento IOS Operating Manual del EN4000X y aportarlo como evidencia para el cierre, o evidenciar que se tiene otro medio alternativo para informar a los usuarios del FSTD.

findings.title: SUB.E5 Apéndice 1 de CS-FSTD(A).300 Estándares FSTD – 1.General.c.1 – Efecto del peso en la dinámica de vuelo
findings.description:
Según el diagrama de peso y centrado de la página de “WEIGHT&SYS” de la IOS y según los límites máximos permisibles para el “Zero Fuel Weight” y para el “Fuel Weight”, es posible seleccionar un peso al despegue de 77.000 kg o más.
Sin embargo, al despegar desde GCFV-Fuerteventura con un peso de 77.000 kg, al avión le costó mucho rotar y elevarse inicialmente con fallo de motor. 
Se recomienda consultar con el fabricante del simulador si el modelo de motor que tiene implementado permite realmente despegar con tanto peso, o si convendría limitar en la IOS el peso máximo al despegue a un valor de 73.500 kg, que suele ser más típico del A320.

En función de la respuesta del fabricante, se valorará la limitación del peso máximo seleccionable en la IOS o la aplicación de la actualización de software que corresponda.
findings.closureEvidence:

findings.title: SUB.B2 Apéndice 1 CS FSTD(A).300 Estándares FSTD-1.General-g.1: Funcionamiento de Sistemas.
findings.description:

findings.title: SUB.E1 Apéndice 1 de CS-FSTD(A).300 Estándares FSTD – 1.General.g.1 – Funcionamiento de Sistemas.
findings.description:
Cuando se fallan ambos generadores de corriente eléctrica, la batería tarda entre 30-40 min en descargarse completamente y dejar al avión sin potencia eléctrica, lo que es correcto.
Sin embargo, la única indicación de descarga de la batería que se tiene es la de los amperios. El voltaje de la batería permanece siempre constante alrededor de los 14 volt dentro de la zona amarilla, durante los 30-40 min de duración de la batería, hasta que de repente se apagan todos los instrumentos.
Se recomienda solicitar al fabricante del simulador que mejore el efecto de la simulación de descarga de la batería, simulando que el voltaje de la batería vaya disminuyendo poco a poco con el paso del tiempo y que la batería se quede sin potencia al llegar la indicación de voltaje a la zona roja del indicador, como si ocurre en otros modelos del simulador ENTROL EN1000 MEP.
NOTA: es una recomendación de mejora pero se espera que la Organización FSTD indique si la va a tener en cuenta o, en caso contrario, que justifique por qué no la va a considerar.
findings.resolution: La Organización FSTD acepta la recomendación y ha trasladado en día 21/07/2026 la incidencia al fabricante del simulador para solicitar la mejora del modelo de simulación de la batería, de forma que la indicación de voltaje disminuya progresivamente durante la descarga hasta alcanzar la zona roja antes de la pérdida total de alimentación eléctrica. La implantación de esta mejora dependerá de su inclusión en una futura actualización del software del fabricante.
findings.closureEvidence:
10-08-2026
SE ACEPTA Y SE CIERRA

Si es posible, sería deseable tener evidencia de la respuesta del fabricante del simulador, sobre si corregirá, en una versión futura del software, que la indicación de voltaje de la batería vaya disminuyendo hasta la zona roja, a medida que se vaya descargando.

Respuesta Fabricante en el Bug Tracking 
05/08/26 - CORRECTED
“Con un doble fallo de alternador, se simula una reducción en el voltaje de la batería, que caerá de 14V a 12V. No se simula una reducción gradual.
El comportamiento se considera adecuado para un nivel FNPT II y para entrenamiento procedimientos asociados a fallos eléctricos."

findings.title: SUB.E2 Apéndice 1 de CS-FSTD(A).300 Estándares FSTD – 1.General.g.1 – Funcionamiento de Sistemas.
findings.description:
Para que funcione correctamente el poder volar una aproximación PBN del tipo LPV en la zona de las Islas Canarias, es necesario tener seleccionadas en el GARMIN como activas las tres constelaciones de satélites SBAS de “corrección” de señal: EGNOS, WAAS y MSAS. 
Si en el GARMIN sólo se selecciona como activa la constelación EGNOS, entonces las aproximaciones LPV aparecen como “unavailable” en el listado disponible de aproximaciones.
Se recomienda consultar con el fabricante del simulador si este funcionamiento del GARMIN es el correcto.
NOTA: es una recomendación de mejora pero se espera que la Organización FSTD indique si la va a tener en cuenta o, en caso contrario, que justifique por qué no la va a considerar.
findings.resolution: La Organización FSTD acepta la recomendación y ha trasladado en día 21/07/2026 la consulta al fabricante del simulador para verificar si el comportamiento observado es conforme al funcionamiento previsto del equipo Garmin y de las aproximaciones LPV en la región de Canarias. En caso de confirmarse una discrepancia, se solicitará la correspondiente corrección mediante una futura actualización del software.
findings.closureEvidence:
10-08-2026
SE ACEPTA
PENDIENTE DE EVIDENCIA PARA CIERRE
Si es posible, sería deseable tener evidencia de la respuesta del fabricante del simulador, sobre si es correcto el comportamiento del GARMIN en lo referente a qué constelaciones SBAS deben estar activadas para poder volar una aproximación LPV en la región de Canarias.

Suponiendo que se confirme que sea un fallo de cómo está simulado el comportamiento del receptor GNSS/GARMIN por parte del fabricante, y que éste procederá a su corrección en una versión software futura, en ese caso se debería evidenciar que el fallo está anotado en el HIL-Listado de Diferidos mientras dure.

Respuesta Organización FSTD 10-08-2026:
Se ha intentado reproducir el fallo, sin embargo, el sistema funciona correctamente. Al quitar todas las constelaciones de SBAS, los procedimientos LPV aparecen como UNAVAIL, y al seleccionar solo EGNOS, vuelven a estar disponibles. Se adjunta video “SUB.E2 MEP LPV Approach Database with EGNOS”
